## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1415775e6f78a8133a697304e67a8ef03ba6b5a1`
Local-runs: probe — the ratchet self-test on the head worktree is the one measurement of the re-pin against the live `bootstrap.md` (writer bytes = reader bytes, hand audit = priced count) that CI's green does not print.
Probe detail: `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs --self-test` in a detached worktree at the head, no install: exit 0, "104 cases pass", all seven body-pin rows ✓. Everything else was read, not run (the hand audit below is `wc -c` / `grep` over the tree, the header's own formula applied by hand).
Scope: scripts/check-skill-compatibility-version.mjs (claim) + .github/workflows/release.yml, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs (by ruling B, triage record 6730018726)

Inputs read: card #31115 (body; comments 6706623953 triage, 6708443569 ruling A on item 1, 6718198041 claim, 6718224824 decision owed with the dev's four-option analysis, 6718947788 and 6719355267 items 1–2 report and landing, 6730018726 ruling B of record for item 3, 6730391223 os-dev-report for this PR), PR #31745 body and file list (3 files, +626 −46, every patch present), `git diff f2abd4767 1415775e` against the live tree at the head (worktree), the seat's project files `issue-31115/` (item3-needs-decision.md, item3.patch, pr-body-item3.md, pr-body.md), and the check-runs on the head twice. At the second read: 58 check-runs, 54 concluded — 42 success (`Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Type Check · source gates` — the lane that runs `pnpm check:skill-compatibility` at lint.yml:5402 and the ratchet self-test + scan at lint.yml:5490–5491 — `Type Check · workspace`, every `Lint ·` lane, `Test Core (2/8)`, all 16 `Test UI` shards), 11 expected skips, and ONE red: `Check Changeset`, red because the PR carries no `skip-changeset` label (labels at read time: `ci/cd`, `size/l`; the step's own log: "Check Changeset is not one of the required contexts"). 4 still `in_progress` (`Build & E2E UI`, `Lint UI`, `Test Core (1/8)`, `Type Check UI`), none of which exercises the three changed files. "Every check green" is the landing condition, not this record's; the seat re-reads it before landing, and ② names what makes `Check Changeset` green.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Surface = claim + ruling, nothing more.** Three files: `scripts/check-skill-compatibility-version.mjs` is in the claim (6718198041: "body versions + `--fix`"); `.github/workflows/release.yml` and `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` are the two the ruling names (6730018726 "Two files are outside the original surface"). No `skills/**` file, no `package.json`, no `lint.yml` line, no changeset (`bootstrap.md` 190 → 190 lines, 5398 bytes, unchanged on the head). The ruling's "merge `main` after #31335 lands" is satisfied by construction: the branch was cut from `f2abd476`, which already carries #31335 (the ratchet's CEILINGS hunk this PR edits is one row, :1275, and the diff applies cleanly to that basis). **Right.**
- **Tier H by path.** `release.yml` is in `WORKFLOW_TIER_H_FILES` (check-governed-merges.mjs:1631, "publishes the packages"), so the split reader cannot lower it; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded success and the PR body says a governed approver's APPROVED review is owed. **Right.**
- **Accept set: the sixth filter widens only what `--fix` legitimately writes.** `BODY_LIST` (release.yml:746) is resolved from `bodyPinnedPaths()` (compat:814), which is the WRITER asked with a probe (`BODY_PROBE`, :791): a file is listed iff `deriveBodyVersions` (:469) would move at least one byte of it for some version, i.e. it carries a non-history body version. The version pass writes a file iff `deriveBodyVersions` with the real workspace moves a byte of it — a subset of the listed set (the probe also counts an already-current value, which is the point: the guard runs AFTER the pass, when every value is current; and a value naming a package the workspace lacks, which `--fix` leaves alone and the check reds at compat:434–438, so no green tree carries one). Nothing else is newly admitted: the filter is `grep -vxF -f` (whole-line, fixed-string, :763), the same mechanism as the four lists above it, so no path outside the list can match, and admission is whole-file at the same granularity as `SKILL_LIST`. **Right.**
- **Empty-list case is fail-safe.** `bodyPinnedPaths()` THROWS on a tree with no skill markdown (compat:816–823, "a moved directory") → the `node -e` resolve exits non-zero → `exit 1` (release.yml:750–751). It returns `[]` only on a catalog with markdown and no pins → an empty `BODY_LIST` → `grep -vxF -f <empty>` matches nothing, `-v` passes every line, so nothing is admitted: the body write that would then be unexpected IS reported. The deliberate absence of the `[ ! -s ]` check the other four lists carry is therefore correct, and the comment at :742 says why. If the extractor regressed to list nothing, `bootstrap.md` would surface as `unexpected` — the failure direction is red. Pinned: 'a body-pin write is admitted by the bodyPinnedPaths() filter alone, and an empty body list admits nothing' (compat:1511–1539, real `grep` via `spawnSync`). **Right.**
- **Ratchet: the unpriced rule reaches only writer-rewritten values, with no general escape hatch.** `pricedTokens(text, {bodyPinned})` (:1463) subtracts `bodyPinValues(text).bytes` only when `run()` found the file in `bodyPinnedPaths()` (:1665). `bodyPinValues` (:1408) hands the file to the SAME writer with a probe and prices back exactly the bytes it replaced (old line − new line + probes × probe bytes), throwing if the writer changed the line count. So the unpriced bytes are the version VALUES only; the package name, quotes, `^`/`~`, the key, every history version and every other byte stay priced — pinned by 'the unpriced body bytes are exactly the version values the writer owns, never a range, name or history version' (count 2, bytes 12 on a fixture with a `^` pin and a `Removed in … 16.0.0` sentence) and, on the live file, by 'on every real body-pinned file the unpriced bytes are exactly the non-history versions the reader finds'. An author cannot buy headroom: each extra pin costs ~30 priced bytes to shed ≤ 15, and a pin naming a non-existent package reds `check:skill-compatibility` in the same lane. **Right.**
- **Width.** `stampWidths` (:1946) is `17.7.0, 18.0.0-next.0, 18.9.0, 18.10.0, 18.10.0-next.12, 100.0.0`; 'a body pin change of any width moves no count (18.3.0 -> 18.10.0-next.12)' asserts one priced count across the whole set, and 'one authored byte over a zero-headroom body-pinned ceiling is red at every pin width' holds the ceiling tight at every width. The width trap the ruling names (18.9 → 18.10, `-next`) is closed and pinned. **Right.**
- **The re-pin 1351 → 1343 is measured and legitimate under the ratchet's own conventions.** Hand audit with the header's own formula (:135–138) on the head's `bootstrap.md`: 5398 bytes, five `18.3.0` values = 30 bytes, `ceil(5398/4)` = 1350 priced whole, `ceil(5368/4)` = 1342 with the values out. Old row 1351 at count 1350 = headroom 1; new row 1343 at count 1342 = headroom 1 — lowered by exactly the 8 the count fell, as `BODY_PIN_REPIN` (:356, basis `f2abd476`, pins 5, value `18.3.0`, tokens 8) records and as 'the body-pin re-pin is recorded' pins. This is the `STAMP_LINE_REPIN` precedent ("re-pinned, never loosened") applied verbatim. Probe: 104 cases pass on the head, including 'the header's hand audit reproduces every real body-pinned count'. **Right.**
- **The history rule and the writer agree.** `HISTORY_RE` (:383) decides both `judgeBodyVersions` (prose only — an install pin is "always judged", :446) and `deriveBodyVersions` (a history prose version is left alone, :472–476). The catalog carries six body versions: five install pins in `bootstrap.md` and one prose version at `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/record-page.md:44` ("were removed in @objectstack/spec 18.3.0") — read on the head, `removed in` matches, so that file is history-only, not listed, not written, priced whole. The PR body's "6 body version(s) in 71 skill markdown file(s)" and the one-file `BODY_PIN_REPIN` agree with the tree. **Right.**
- **Public surface.** New exports from the compat script: `extractBodyVersions`, `judgeBodyVersions`, `deriveBodyVersions`, `readSkillMarkdown`, `bodyPinnedPaths`; `applyFix` gains a defaulted fourth parameter and returns `{ files, markdown, written }` (one new key; the self-test is its only consumer). From the ratchet: `bodyPinValues`, `BODY_PIN_REPIN`; `pricedTokens` gains an optional `bodyPinned` (default preserves every caller). Repo scripts, not a published package. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

The diff touches two repo scripts and one workflow; no `packages/**`, no `skills/**`, no published entry point, no changeset edited or added. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body; `check-changeset-no-major` concluded "no `major` bump … a non-protocol change at `patch`". **Correct level.** The posture is `skip-changeset` — route 2 of the Check Changeset message (this PR releases nothing; the route-0 discriminator does not apply because no `.changeset/*.md` row is `M` or `D`) — **but the label is not on the PR**, which is the one red on the head. The dev's `writes: 2` kept labels to the seat, per the dispatch order ("comments, labels and bodies only via `scripts/pm` write tools"). **Landing item L1:** the seat applies `skip-changeset` through `scripts/pm` before landing; the gate re-reads labels live and goes green without a push. No grade on the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **B1 (`Check Changeset` red, label missing).** Named in ② as L1. Not a defect of the diff; a seat write owed before landing. Answered.
- **B2 (dev flag: the branch was restarted from `main` after #31432 and `item3.patch` re-applied as 79468c32).** Read: `79468c32` is the reader/history rule/`deriveBodyVersions` and `1415775e` the `--fix`/guard/ratchet half; both are on the branch, no history rewrite, and `item3.patch` in the project files matches the first commit's substance. Answered: no effect on the record.
- **B3 (`--fix` and the unpriced set reach non-history PROSE versions, not only install pins).** The card (item 3) and the ruling's first clause say "`--fix` rewrites the install-shape body pins"; the diff's writer (:469) also rewrites a prose version that does not read as history, and the ratchet then unprices it. This is a reasoned extension, not a breach: the check's contract ("equal or history") makes every non-history prose version a statement of the CURRENT version, so at version time a check-only prose version would red `check:skill-compatibility` in `release.yml`'s content half (:815) — the same "check-only is not an option" fact that forced the decision. Today the catalog carries zero such values (the one prose version is history), so nothing on this tree changes hands. **For the maintainer's eye, no grade:** at a release, a sentence such as "Install @objectstack/spec 18.3.0" in any skill body is rewritten by the bot, as the `metadata.version` stamp is. If that is unwanted, the narrowing is one line (`shape === 'install'` in `to()` at :476) and the check's prose arm would need to accept "equal to ANY past release" — a different rule from the card's.
- **B4 (self-test fragility, fail-closed).** 'the header's hand audit reproduces every real body-pinned count' (:2010–2011) requires every live body-pinned file to carry ONLY install pins (`allInstall`), because the header's `grep | sed` formula reads install pins alone. The day an author writes a legitimate non-history prose version into a body-pinned file, the ratchet SELF-TEST reds (not the gate), with a message that names the file but not the cause. Red direction, same convention as the ratchet's other live-tree pins (`skillMdOnDisk`, `notTheStamp`). Nit N1 below.
- **B5 (platform tier).** The dev-report says `dispatch-gates --tier` derived no mandate for these paths and the default tier was used; the earlier PR's clause-① mandate was for `skills/**`, which this PR does not touch. Answered.

### ④ Design judgment

**`release.yml` (:739–764), sentence by sentence against the ruling's second clause ("a new written-set export is declared to release.yml's post-version guard").** The export is `bodyPinnedPaths()`, declared where the other four rewriters' sets are, resolved the same way (`node --input-type=module -e 'import …'` from the repo root — the module's entry-point guard, `isEntrypoint`, already serves `stampedSkillPaths` on :728 so the import is side-effect-free), filtered the same way (whole-line fixed match), and judged by the content gate that already runs (`run_gate pnpm check:skill-compatibility`, :815, which now judges bodies). The comment header is edited from "Five filters … four declared lists" to "Six … five" and is true. The one deliberate difference from its neighbours (no empty-file refusal) is argued in the comment and holds under ① ("Empty-list case"). **Holds.** A note on granularity, pre-existing and shared with `SKILL_LIST`: admission is per FILE, so a second version-time writer that later learns to touch `bootstrap.md` would be admitted by this list without a new declaration. Not this diff's to fix; worth remembering when the next rewriter arrives.

**`check-skill-compatibility-version.mjs`, the body section (:349–506) and the writer (:790–872).**

- *Reader.* Two shapes, both anchored on `@objectstack/<pkg>` and a full `x.y.z[-pre]`: an `N.x` pin, a bare `18.3.0`, a table cell `| 18.3.0 |` are not read (pinned: 'frontmatter pins and the stamp are not body versions'). Frontmatter is skipped by `frontmatterEnd`; fenced code is deliberately NOT skipped (the starter package.json is the target). The sentence a prose match sits in is rebuilt across wrapped lines (`sentenceAt`, :405–415) and `HISTORY_RE` is tested on that sentence, so "removed in" one line above still counts and "one sentence away" does not — both pinned. **Holds.**
- *Judge.* Equal → green; prose + history → green; install pin is always judged; unknown package → red with its own message; the red names `file:line`, both versions and the `--fix` command. **Holds.**
- *Writer.* `deriveBodyVersions` rewrites every non-history version to its package's version and keeps `^`/`~`; a second pass is a no-op; it never touches the frontmatter — all pinned. `applyFix` (:839) derives frontmatter first, body second on the derived text, writes each file ONCE, and hands the check the derived text for both halves. **Holds.** One divergence between judge and writer, contrived enough to be a nit: the history set (:472) is keyed `line:pkg:version`, so on a single line carrying BOTH a prose history mention and an install pin of the same package at the same version (`Since … removed in @objectstack/spec 18.3.0: "@objectstack/spec": "18.3.0"`), the install pin is not rewritten although the judge says an install pin is always judged. Nit N2.
- *Export.* `bodyPinnedPaths` throws on no markdown, `[]` on no pins, lists by the writer's probe; 'bodyPinnedPaths() on the live tree is exactly the files the reader finds a non-history version in' cross-checks writer against reader on the real catalog. The self-test's written-set case is now `stampedSkillPaths() then bodyPinnedPaths()` in walk order against what `applyFix` wrote on an all-stale fixture with a pinned file and a history-only file, and asserts the body is green afterwards and the history file untouched. **Holds.**
- *Floor.* `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` 30 → 44 with 14 new rows, each declared in `SELF_TEST_BATTERIES` and each registered by the driving loop. **Holds.**

**`check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`: the second exclusion (:116–138 header; :356; :1408–1475; :1665–1690; the seven self-test rows).** The header's rule is now stated as ONE rule with TWO exclusions ("bytes the version script writes are not priced"), which is exactly the ruling's "generalising the frontmatter stamp-line rule"; the first exclusion's text is kept and its "Nothing else moves" sentence is amended to point at the second. The writer-asked-with-a-probe pattern is reused rather than a second parser, so the ratchet cannot disagree with `--fix` about which bytes are derived. The report line names the unpriced byte count on a body-pinned row, as it does for the stamp. **Holds.** Two nits on the self-test, neither a contract effect:

- **N1** (B4) — 'the header's hand audit reproduces every real body-pinned count' conflates "the formula reproduces the count" with "every owned version is an install pin". When that assumption breaks the self-test reds for a reason the message does not name. Fix: split it — keep `pinHandAuditMisses` over the `allInstall` files only, and add a row asserting the current fact (`realBodyPinned.every(allInstall)`) with a label that says so.
- **N2** — `deriveBodyVersions`'s same-line history key (compat:472, :476) can shield an install pin; the judge never does. Fix: compute the history set from PROSE matches only (it already is) and skip the `history.has` test inside the install-pin replacer.
- **N3** — `repinMisses` (:1984–1986) still calls `pricedTokens(text)` with no options for a non-stamped file and so prices `bootstrap.md` whole; its comment "every other file must read exactly as it did" is no longer what `run()` does for that file. The new row 'on every real body-pinned file …' carries the body-pinned case, so nothing is unguarded; the older row's comment is now narrower than its words. A one-line comment fix.

**The simulated release** in the PR body (five packages set to `18.10.0-next.12`, 12 files rewritten, 0 unexpected with the list and 1 without, ratchet 1342 / 1343, restored) is the only exercise of the release lane this PR can have before a Version Packages PR; it is consistent with every reading above and with the probe.

**Verdict reasoning.** The surface is the claim plus exactly the two files the ruling names. The guard's sixth filter admits only what the writer owns, whole-line, and fails red on a throw, on an empty list and on a regressed extractor. The ratchet unprices only the bytes the same writer replaces, pinned on fixtures and on the live file, and the re-pin is the stamp-line precedent applied with the arithmetic right (5398 → 5368, 1350 → 1342, headroom 1 → 1). Width `18.9 → 18.10` and `-next` are pinned on both sides. Semver and changeset posture are right in the diff; the `skip-changeset` label is a seat write owed before landing (L1). The three nits are self-test prose and a contrived writer edge, none of which lets a wrong value land green or a right one land red on a real tree. No must-fix.
